PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Respondent(s) No. 1  ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE NIKHIL S. KARIEL  Date : 30/03/2026
ORAL ORDER
Draft amendment is allowed.
To be carried out forthwith.

1. Heard learned advocate Mr. Jagat Patel appearing on behalf of the applicant and learned Additional Public Prosecutor Mr. J.K. Shah appearing on behalf of the respondent-State.
2. Rule.
Learned APP waives service of rule on behalf of the respondent-State.

3. The applicant has filed this application under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Chetankumar Balubhai Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 30 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161058927/
1 Sanhita, 2023 for enlarging the applicant on Regular Bail in connection with FIR being C.R. No.
11191067250020 of 2025 registered with Cyber Crime Police Station, Ahmedabad, for the offence punishable under Sections 406, 420, 120-B of the Indian Penal Code and Section 66(c) and 66(d) of the I.T. Act.

sentences.text: 4. Learned advocate for the applicant would submit that considering the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/6992/2026 ORDER DATED: 30/03/2026 undefined role attributed to the applicant, and nature of the allegation levelled, the applicant may be enlarged on regular bail.
It is further submitted that since the charge-sheet is filed no useful purpose would be served by keeping the applicant in jail for indefinite period.
It is further contended that the applicant is ready and willing to abide by all the conditions that may be imposed by this Court if released on bail.
5. As against the same, learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent - State has vehemently objected to the grant of regular bail.

Learned APP has submitted that looking to the nature of offence and the role attributed to the present applicant as coming out from the charge- sheet, this Court may not exercise the discretion in favour of the applicant and the application may be dismissed.
6.
I have heard learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties and perused the papers.
Following aspects are considered:-

(i) The allegation being that the accused had defrauded the complainant and other persons by involving them in Telegram group and asking them to perform certain tasks for which certain amount to be given as commission and whereas the complainant and others were lured to deposit large sums and whereas the amount having come to the account of the applicant and the same had been siphoned off by the other accused.
(ii) The fact of the account having been opened by the co-accused in the name of the present applicant.
(iii) The fact of the said account being used by co-accused.

While it is alleged that a t o t a l o f R s . 1 , 4 0 , 0 0 , 0 0 0 / - h a d c o m e t o t h e N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N R/CR.MA/6992/2026 ORDER DATED: 30/03/2026 undefined account in question and around 45 complaints were registered in the NCCRP portal, yet it would also appear very clearly that the account was not opened by the present applicant rather it was opened by a co-accused.

(iv) It also appears that the co-accused Nayan, who was instrumental in opening the account, had been released on regular bail by the learned Sessions Court and whereas it would appear that the learned Sessions Court had taken into consideration a contention that no money had been come to the account of the said accused, though prima facie, it would appear that there was no allegation against the said accused of having provided his account.

sentences.text: (v) Be that as it may, it would appear that since the role attributed to the present applicant is very limited and since it also appears very clearly that the applicant had received in all a commission of Rs.10,000/-, though around 45 complaints have been registered in the NCCRP Portal, yet this Court is inclined to consider this application having regard to the prima facie opinion of this Court that the present applicant does not appear to be involved even insofar as giving him account for the purpose of laundering money.
(vi) This Court has also taken into account the fact that the applicant was arrested on 10.12.2025, charge-sheet has been filed and the applicant having no antecedents.

This Court has taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation reported in [2012] 1 SCC 40.
7.

sentences.text: In the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the nature NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/6992/2026 ORDER DATED: 30/03/2026 undefined of the allegations made against the applicant in the First Information Report, without discussing the evidence in detail, prima facie, this Court is of the opinion that this is a fit case to exercise the discretion and enlarge the applicant on regular bail.
8. Hence, the present application is allowed.

[d] not leave the State of Gujarat without prior permission of the Sessions Court concerned;
[e] furnish the present address of residence to the I.O. and also to the Court at the time of execution of the b6067ond and shall not change the residence without prior intimation to the I.O.;
[f] mark presence once a month for a period of six months before the concerned police station.
9. The Authorities will release the applicant only if he is not required in connection with any other offence for the time being.
If breach of any of the above conditions is committed, the Sessions Court concerned will be free to take appropriate action in the matter.
